title.narrative: Supporting Populations at Risk of Famine with Multipurpose Cash Assistance

description.narrative: The conflict in Sudan has severely impacted food security and livelihoods, with 86 per cent of IDPs citing food and 77 per cent citing livelihoods as priority needs, according to IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) (August 2024). While food is available in some areas, inflation and loss of livelihoods have made it unaffordable for many – 90 per cent of DTM respondents across the country say that food is available where they live, but it is unaffordable. In Khartoum and West Darfur, 93 and 100 percent respectively cite food as a priority need, above the national average.Over half of the population (25.6 million people) faced crisis or worse levels (IPC Level 3 or above) between June and September 2023, coinciding with the lean season. In the IPC Acute Food Insecurity Snapshot (April 2024 – February 2025), 14 states, including Khartoum and West Darfur, are at risk of famine, increasing risks of health complications, mortality, protection risks such as gender-based violence and exploitation, and harmful coping strategies such as skipping meals, selling assets, and borrowing money.To address these needs, IOM will provide multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) to 3370 households (around 18,370 individuals) in Sirba, Kereneik, and Khartoum localities, enabling them to meet their urgent basic needs. Cash was chosen as the preferred means of distribution according to beneficiaries’ preferences, based on feedback collected from previous interventions. As markets are functioning in the targeted intervention areas, cash will allow beneficiaries to fill gaps in their households based on their own individual assessment, allowing for more effective and improved outputs when compared to in-kind assistance. 3,000 households averaging six members (giving a total of 18,000 beneficiaries) will receive $450 (three monthly payments based on $150 a month), covering 70 per cent of the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB), as per the Cash Working Group (CWG) standards. In addition, 370 vulnerable individuals will receive $78 (three monthly payments based on a $26 a month, covering 70 per cent of the MEB for a single person) in line with CWG standards. Target beneficiaries will be 1700 households and 210 additional individuals in Khartoum, and 1300 households and 160 additional individuals in West Darfur. Cash will be distributed through local partners, enhancing access to hard-to-reach areas. IOM will explore the possibility of distribution through mobile money transfers, subject to the functionality of Financial Service Provider (FSP) platforms and the preferences of the affected populations. otherwise, the assistance will be distributed in a cash-in-hand modality through FSPs, partners, or through IOM staff as a last resort. This cash assistance, aligned with the 2024 Famine Prevention Plan and the Humanitarian Response Plan, focuses on displaced and vulnerable populations, and will be distributed in a conflict-sensitive manner.
